newsitem.title: HONG KONG: DHL Int'l sees 35-40 pct growth in China.
newsitem.headline: DHL Int'l sees 35-40 pct growth in China.

text.p: A DHL International (Hong Kong) Ltd official said on Tuesday he expects the air express giant's China operations to grow by at least 35-40 percent this year.

"That's very conservative," Andy Tseng, area manager for Hong Kong and China told Reuters. "This kind of express is quite new in China and we continue to add new offices to provide the ground for this business to develop."

The parcel and freight handler holds 28 percent of the Chinese market through its DHL-Sinotrans Ltd 50-50 joint venture with the Chinese foreign trade transport company Sinotrans, Tseng earlier told a press conference.
DHL-Sinotrans, which offers both international air express and domestic courier services, was developing its network within China, he said.

The joint venture opened its 20th Chinese office in Hefei in the eastern province of Anhui province on January 8 and will open a branch in Suzhou in neighbouring Jiangsu province on January 18, Tseng said.
He said DHL-Sinotrans plans to have 31 to 35 offices in China by the end of 1997.

The only impediment to the company's growth in China was a lack of infrastructure, which slowed the movement of cargo, Tseng told Reuters. He said he hoped improvements would be made at a faster pace.
"That way people will appreciate the premium service of this express industry," he said. "If you don't have infrastructure then what's the difference -- there's no difference."
Tseng said current trends show that the bulk of most air express shipments will be made up of clothing and textiles, electrical machinery and telecommunications.
He said the busiest destinations would be Asia in general and China in particular.
DHL International is a unit of DHL Worldwide Express.
